principle: Morphological case is an explicit local gauge of semantic role; case-less languages encode the same role through word order, adpositions, clitics, agreement, and verb valency.

pl.notes: Polish case morphology carries role and operator information directly on nominal forms.

en.notes: English maps many case roles to position and prepositions.

de.notes: German is not case-less; it is a bridge language with reduced but active case morphology.

fr.notes: French maps case roles to prepositions, clitics and rigid syntax.

es.notes: Spanish uses prepositions, clitics, agreement and differential object marking for some role distinctions.

case_roles.pl_marking: morphological case ending; adjective/determiner agreement; often lemma/citation form
case_roles.en_strategy: subject position before finite verb; nominative pronouns he/she/they/I/we
case_roles.de_strategy: nominative articles/pronouns plus subject agreement; flexible order with case marking
case_roles.fr_strategy: subject position and clitic/tonic subject pronouns
case_roles.es_strategy: subject agreement on verb, optional explicit subject, word order/pragmatics

case_roles.pl_marking: morphological case ending; animacy/gender interactions; verb valency
case_roles.en_strategy: direct object position after transitive verb; object pronouns him/her/them/me/us
case_roles.fr_strategy: direct object NP after verb or object clitic position before finite verb
case_roles.es_strategy: direct object NP, personal a for human/animate specific objects, clitics

case_roles.pl_marking: morphological case ending; governed by many prepositions, numerals, negation, possession
case_roles.en_strategy: of-phrase, possessive 's, from, some/any/no, partitive expressions; sometimes word order
case_roles.de_strategy: genitive for possession/formal register; von + dative in colloquial; governed prepositions
case_roles.fr_strategy: de phrase for possession/source/partitive; articles du/de la/des; negation often de
case_roles.es_strategy: de phrase for possession/source/partitive; partitive/negative expressed lexically
case_roles.example_en: I do not have water / I have no water.

case_roles.pl_marking: morphological case ending; verb/adjective valency; recipient/beneficiary roles
case_roles.de_strategy: dative articles/pronouns; indirect object; governed prepositions
case_roles.fr_strategy: à phrase or indirect object clitics lui/leur
case_roles.es_strategy: a/para phrase or indirect object clitics le/les
case_roles.example_en: I give water to the child / I give the child water.

case_roles.de_strategy: mit/durch/von/als phrases, often dative after prepositions
case_roles.example_en: I write with a pen / using a pen.

case_roles.pl_marking: morphological case ending; normally appears with prepositions such as w, na, o, po, przy
case_roles.en_strategy: in/on/at/about/after/near phrases selected by lexical operator
case_roles.de_strategy: in/an/auf/über/bei plus dative or accusative depending on static/directional role

case_roles.pl_marking: morphological case ending; often proper names/animate nouns; speech act role
case_roles.en_strategy: bare name/noun with comma, intonation, O/hey in marked registers
case_roles.de_strategy: bare name/noun with comma/intonation; no productive vocative morphology
case_roles.fr_strategy: name/noun with comma/intonation; ô in literary register
case_roles.es_strategy: name/noun with comma/intonation; oye/oh in marked contexts

formal_maps.encode: RoleOperator(x, role) -> Surface_l(x, word_order, adposition, clitic, agreement)
formal_maps.cross_language_equivalence: Equivalent(S_l1,S_l2) iff CaseRoleInvariant(S_l1) == CaseRoleInvariant(S_l2) and predicate-argument structure is preserved.
